Current means of classifying electroactive versus spectator molecules are insufficient, while improvement of ink formulations, depositions, and distributions relies primarily on indirect links to electrochemical performance. In this study, we expand the common utilization of Cyclic Voltammetry (CV) in homogeneous systems toward heterogenized molecular catalyst architectures. We illustrate how, even with porous catalyst layers containing carbon, ionomer, and molecules, a combined redox wave integration and UV-vis analysis can be used as a tool for designing a reproducible deposition procedure. An in-depth CV analysis is then used to study the effect of catalyst aggregation and quantify the number of electroactive sites on carbon supports. We show that FeTPP (Iron(III)meso-tetraphenylporphyrin chloride) gives a non-linear electroactive response when loading is varied, allowing for the identification of distinct loading regions of insufficient, optimal, and excessive coverage. A FeTPP to Vulcan carbon mass ratio of 0.1 provides the highest number of electroactive species, giving the lowest expected aggregation. Overall, the CV approaches are extendable to any redox-active catalysts, providing a versatile means of characterizing porous heterogeneous molecular catalyst systems.
10.1002_anie.202521363: The co‐electrolysis of nitrate (NO 3 − ) and carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) to synthesize urea can satisfy the comprehensive needs of carbon footprint closure, waste valorization, and sustainable urea production. However, designing efficient electrocatalysts to promote the electrocatalytic C─N coupling process and achieve efficient urea production remains a challenge. Here, we design a copper (Cu)‐based coordination polymer catalyst, which can achieve the dual function of promoting C─N coupling and protonation through sulfur (S)‐coordinated adjacent Cu sites. Through the unique Continuous Coupling Mechanism (CCM) of low Gibbs free energy of reaction intermediates (*CO 2 + *NO to *CO 2 NO to *ONCO 2 NO), the resulting catalyst achieved ultra‐high Faradaic efficiency (FE) (84.9 ± 3.1%) and production rate (0.34 ± 0.012 mol h −1 g −1 ). Moreover, the FE and production rate of urea did not change noticeably during at least 90 cycles of testing.
10.1002_smll.72943: Material degradation in layered oxide cathodes, particularly mechanical degradation, presents a “chicken or egg” dilemma as it may originate from either the surface or the bulk. Surface‐only or bulk‐only modifications have proven insufficient to resolve these intrinsic issues. While combined surface‐bulk strategies can mitigate degradation, they often require complex processes that increase costs and limit scalability. Here, we report a design that couples bulk structural stabilization with the in situ formation of a fast conductive interphase on Ni‐rich layered oxides. This dual approach yields a robust bulk framework and a stable surface with accelerated reaction kinetics, enabling a high‐rate capability of over 160 mAh g −1 at the current of 5 C and stable cycling over 200 cycles. Beyond performance gains, our results reveal atomic‐scale insights into the interplay between structural evolution, ionic transport, and electrochemical stability, offering a practical pathway to durable high‐nickel cathodes for fast‐charging batteries.
10.1016_j.jece.2026.123351: Ozonation represents a promising mild-condition biorefinery strategy for oxidative valorization of biomass-derived alkenes. However, it suffers from oxidative decomposition, resulting in product loss. A deep understanding of such decomposition is crucial for designing efficient conversion pathways that suppress overoxidation, especially when phenolic compounds are involved. In this study, we systematically screened nearly one hundred monomeric and dimeric phenols and methylated analogs to explore the structure-reactivity relationship during ozonation. We found the substrate structure significantly influenced decomposition reactivity, leading to rate differences exceeding two orders of magnitude. Some phenols are completely inert toward O 3 , while certain non-phenolic derivatives undergo rapid oxidation. Ozonation of para-substituted phenols follows Hammett equation. The decomposition of guaiacol-type phenols selectively yields value-added monomethyl muconates. Among solvents, tetrahydrofurfuryl alcohol exhibits significant stabilizing and protective functions, enhancing product yield and mitigating overoxidation. Integrating methylation pretreatment and tetrahydrofurfuryl alcohol, we achieved the high-yield of methylated vanillin (88%) and methylated syringaldehyde (96%) via ozonation of methylated lignin depolymerization products, showcasing an efficient ozone-based valorization pathway. Collectively, this work provides fundamental insights of ozonation of phenolic derivatives, validates the efficient production of lignin-derived aromatic aldehydes at mild conditions, and highlights the great potential of ozone-based technologies for advanced biorefinery.
10.1016_j.tra.2026.105201: New energy bus (NEB) technologies, including battery electric buses (BEBs) and hydrogen fuel cell buses (FCBs), offer pathways to support decarbonisation strategies in public transport. Selecting the most suitable technology represents a multi-dimensional decision problem encompassing trade-offs across different criteria. This paper provides a comprehensive review of the factors influencing the choice of BEBs or FCBs, grouped into technological, economic, managerial, social, environmental, and institutional categories. We address this NEB technology selection problem using a hybrid multi-criteria decision-making framework integrating the Best-Worst Method (BWM) and the Measurement of Alternatives and Ranking according to Compromise Solution (MARCOS). Evaluation criteria are identified and refined through a structured expert interview process, and their weights are determined using BWM based on assessments from 34 international experts with diverse backgrounds. The MARCOS method is applied to evaluate and rank NEB alternatives, including BEBs, FCBs, and mixed fleet configurations. Results indicate that economic factors (e.g., vehicle, energy, and infrastructure costs) are the most influential, followed by institutional (e.g., political will and funding) and technological (e.g., driving range and energy system resilience) dimensions. BEBs are identified as the most suitable option for current urban systems, while FCBs remain competitive where operational flexibility is critical. Interestingly, a divergence is observed between academic and industry perspectives, with the former prioritising economic and environmental factors, whereas the latter prioritise institutional and technological factors. This is also reflected in the ranking of alternatives, with academics favouring BEBs and industry experts favouring FCBs, highlighting the importance of incorporating stakeholder perspectives into decision-making.
10.1021_acssuschemeng.6c00679: Since facet-dependent reaction pathways are frequently disrupted by competitive hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) and reductive reconstruction, precisely controlling the selectivity of the electrocatalytic CO2 reduction reaction (CO2RR) on CuOx-based catalysts remains challenging. In this paper, Cu2O nanoparticles (NPs) with explicitly exposed facets (100), mixed (100)/(111), and (111) were synthesized and further modified with the conductive polypyrrole (PPy) layer through an in-situ polymerization reaction to achieve the synergistic effect of crystal facet engineering and interfacial microenvironment. This approach enabled precise regulation of the CO2RR pathways on the Cu2O NPs. The experimental results showed that the PPy modification enhanced the CO2 adsorption and hydrophobicity, effectively inhibiting HER and promoting the deep reduction of CO2. In the H-type cell with 0.1 mol/L KHCO3 electrolyte saturated with CO2, the Faraday efficiency (FE) of the PPy-c-Cu2O catalyst for the deeply reduced products reached 54.6%, while FEH2 decreased from 43.1 to 17.4%. All PPy-modified Cu2O catalysts with different exposed crystal facets exhibited enhanced CO selectivity in the flow cell. Quasi in-situ X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy showed that PPy modification prevented the active Cu(I) species from being reduced under cathode bias, enhanced stability, and enabled the FE of deeply reduced products to remain at 48.5% over 10 h. Density functional theory calculations indicated that PPy modification increased the *CO coverage on Cu2O (100) facets, reduced the C−C coupling barrier, and suppressed the HER process by raising the *H coupling energy barrier. This work provides experimental and theoretical guidance for the rational design of highly selective Cu2O catalysts.
